text: The area of the polygon, whose vertices are the non-real roots of the equation $z–=iz^{2}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$z–=iz^{2}$

Let $z=x+iy$

$x-iy=i(x^{2}-y^{2}+2xiy)$

$x-iy=i(x^{2}-y^{2})-2xy$

$\therefore$ $x=-2yx$ or $x^{2}-y^{2}=-y$

$x=0$ or $y=-\frac{1}{2}$

Case - I

$x=0$

$-y^{2}=-y$

$y=0,1$

Case - II

$y=-\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow x=\pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$z=\left \{0,i,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{i}{2},\frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{i}{2}\right \}$

Area of polygon $=\frac{1}{2}\left |\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 1 & 1 \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} & \frac{-1}{2} & 1 \\ \frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2} & \frac{-1}{2} & 1 \end{array}\right |$

$=\frac{1}{2}\left |-\sqrt{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right |=\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

$\therefore$ For no solution $α=-\frac{7}{2}$

text: Let a be an integer such that $\lim _{x\to 7}\frac{18-[1-x]}{[x-3a]}$ exists, where [t] is greatest integer $\leq$ t. Then a is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 7}\frac{18-[1-x]}{[x-3a]}$ exist & $a\in I$.

$=\lim _{x\to 7}\frac{17-[-x]}{[x]-3a}$ exist

$RHL=\lim _{x\to 7^{+}}\frac{17-[-x]}{[x]-3a}=\frac{25}{7-3a}$ $\left [a\neq \frac{7}{3}\right ]$

$LHL=\lim _{x\to 7^{-}}\frac{17-[-x]}{[x]-3a}=\frac{24}{6-3a}$ $[a\neq 2]$

For limit to exist

$LHL=RHL$

$\frac{25}{7-3a}=\frac{24}{6-3a}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{25}{7-3a}=\frac{8}{2-a}$

$\therefore$ $a=-6$

text: If $\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{y}{2}\right )=\log _{e}\left (\frac{x}{5}\right )^{5},|y|<2$, then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{y}{2}\right )=\log _{e}\left (\frac{x}{5}\right )^{5}|y|<2$

Differentiating on both side

$-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\left (\frac{y}{2}\right )^{2}}}\times \frac{y^{'}}{2}=\frac{5}{\frac{x}{5}}\times \frac{1}{5}$

$\frac{-xy^{'}}{2}=5\sqrt{1-\left (\frac{y}{2}\right )^{2}}$

Square on both side

$\frac{x^{2}y{}^{'2}}{4}=25\left (\frac{4-y^{2}}{4}\right )$

Diff on both side

$2xy{}^{'2}+2y^{'}y^{''}x^{2}=-25\times 2yy^{'}$

$xy^{'}+y^{''}x^{2}+25y=0$

text: If two straight lines whose direction cosines are given by the relations $l+m-n=0$, $3l^{2}+m^{2}+cnl=0$ are parallel, then the positive value of c is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that the direction cosines satisfy $l+m-n=0$, we find that $n=l+m$.

The other equation is $3l^{2}+m^{2}+cnl=0$, and substituting $n=l+m$ gives $3l^{2}+m^{2}+cl(l+m)=0$.

This simplifies to $(3+c)l^{2}+clm+m^{2}=0$.

As the lines are parallel, they share the same direction ratios, so we can express $l$ in terms of $m$, say $l=km$. Substituting this into our equation gives $(3+c)(km)^{2}+ckm^{2}+m^{2}=0$.

This simplifies to $m^{2}[k^{2}(3+c)+kc+1]=0$.

Since $m\neq 0$, we must have $k^{2}(3+c)+kc+1=0$. Here, we consider the ratio $k=\frac{l}{m}$ to be constant, since the lines are parallel. The equation then becomes a quadratic equation in $k$.

As the lines are parallel, the discriminant of the quadratic equation must be equal to zero for the equation to have equal roots. Hence, the discriminant $D=(c^{2}-4(3+c))=0$.

Solving this quadratic equation gives $c^{2}-4c-12=0$. 

Factoring this equation gives $(c-6)(c+2)=0$.

Solving for $c$ gives $c=6,-2$. 

However, we are looking for the positive value of $c$, so $c=6$.

Therefore, the correct answer is 6
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

text: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}$. Then the number of vectors $\vec{b}$ such that $\vec{b}\times \vec{c}=\vec{a}$ and $|\vec{b}|\in$ {1, 2, ........, 10} is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}=⃗{a}$ to hold, $⃗{a}$ must be perpendicular to $⃗{c}$, because $⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}$ is perpendicular to $⃗{c}$:

$⃗{c}\cdot (⃗{b}\times ⃗{c})=0\Rightarrow ⃗{c}\cdot ⃗{a}=0$

For the given vectors:

$⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}=(1)(2)+(1)(-3)+(-1)(2)=2-3-2=-3\neq 0$

So no vector $⃗{b}$ satisfies $⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}=⃗{a}$, whatever its magnitude, and the number of such vectors is 0.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

text: Let f : R $\to$ R be a function defined by $f(x)=\frac{2e^{2x}}{e^{2x}+e}$. Then $f\left (\frac{1}{100}\right )+f\left (\frac{2}{100}\right )+f\left (\frac{3}{100}\right )+.....+f\left (\frac{99}{100}\right )$ is equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$f(x)=\frac{2e^{2x}}{e^{2x}+e}$

$\therefore$ $f(1-x)=\frac{2e^{2(1-x)}}{e^{2(1-x)}+e}$

$=\frac{2.\frac{e2}{e2x}}{\frac{e2}{e2x}+e}$

$=\frac{2e^{2}}{e^{2}+e^{2x}.e}$

$=\frac{2e^{2}}{e(e+e^{2x})}$

$=\frac{2e}{e+e^{2x}}$

$\therefore$ $f(x)+f(1-x)=\frac{2e^{2x}}{e^{2x}+e}+\frac{2e}{e^{2x}+e}$

$=\frac{2(e^{2x}+e)}{e^{2x}+e}$

$=2$ ...... (1)

Now,

$f\left (\frac{1}{100}\right )+f\left (\frac{99}{100}\right )$

$=f\left (\frac{1}{100}\right )+f\left (1-\frac{1}{100}\right )$

$=2$ [as $f(x)+f(1-x)=2$]

Similarly,

$f\left (\frac{2}{100}\right )+f\left (1-\frac{2}{100}\right )=2$

$\vdots$

$f\left (\frac{49}{100}\right )+f\left (1-\frac{49}{100}\right )=2$

$\therefore$ Total sum $=49\times 2$

Remaining term $=f\left (\frac{50}{100}\right )=f\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )$

Put $x=\frac{1}{2}$ in equation (1), we get

$f\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )+f\left (1-\frac{1}{2}\right )=2$

$\Rightarrow 2f\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=2$

$\Rightarrow f\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=1$

$\therefore$ Sum $=49\times 2+1=99$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

text:
If the sum of all the roots of the equation 

$e^{2x}-11e^{x}-45e^{-x}+\frac{81}{2}=0$ is $\log _{e}p$, then p is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that

$e^{2x}-11e^{x}-45e^{-x}+\frac{81}{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow 2e^{3x}-22e^{2x}-90+81e^{x}=0$

$\Rightarrow 2(e^{x})^{3}-22(e^{x})^{2}+81e^{x}-90=0$

Let $e^{x}=y$

$\Rightarrow 2y^{3}-22y^{2}+81y-90=0$

Product of roots $(y_{1},y_{2},y_{3})$

$y_{1}\cdot y_{2}\cdot y_{3}=\frac{-(-90)}{2}=45$

Let $x_{1},x_{2}$, and $x_{3}$ be roots of given equation

$\Rightarrow e^{x_{1}}\cdot e^{x_{2}}\cdot e^{x_{3}}=45$

$\Rightarrow e^{x_{1}+x_{2}+x_{3}}=45$

$\Rightarrow x_{1}+x_{2}+x_{3}=\log _{e}45=\log _{e}p$

$\Rightarrow p=45$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

text: If the coefficient of $x^{10}$ in the binomial expansion of $\left (\frac{\sqrt{x}}{5^{\dfrac{1}{4}}}+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{x^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}\right )^{60}$ is $5^{k}\quad .l$, where l, k $\in$ N and l is co-prime to 5, then k is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given Binomial Expansion

$=\left (\frac{\sqrt{x}}{5^{\dfrac{1}{4}}}+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{x^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}\right )^{60}$

$\therefore$ General term

$T_{r+1}={}^{60}C_{r}.\left (\frac{x^{1/2}}{5^{1/4}}\right )^{60-r}.\left (\frac{5^{1/2}}{x^{1/3}}\right )^{r}$

$={}^{60}C_{r}.5^{\left (\frac{r}{4}-15+\frac{r}{2}\right )}.x^{\left (30-\frac{r}{2}-\frac{r}{3}\right )}$

$={}^{60}C_{r}.5^{\left (\frac{3r-60}{4}\right )}.x^{\left (\frac{180-5r}{6}\right )}$

For $x^{10}$ term,

$\frac{180-5r}{6}=10$

$\Rightarrow 5r=120$

$\Rightarrow r=24$

$\therefore$ Coefficient of $x^{10}={}^{60}C_{24}.5^{\left (\frac{3\times 24-60}{4}\right )}$

$={}^{60}C_{24}.5^{3}$

$=\frac{60!}{24!36!}.5^{3}$

It is given that,

$\frac{60!}{24!36!}.5^{3}=5^{k}.l$ ...... (1)

Also given that, l is coprime to 5 means l can't be multiple of 5. So we have to find all the factors of 5 in 60!, 24! and 36!

[Note : Formula for exponent or degree of prime number in n!.

Exponent of p in $n!=⌊\frac{n}{p}⌋+⌊\frac{n}{p^{2}}⌋+⌊\frac{n}{p^{3}}⌋+$ ..... until 0 comes

here p is a prime number. ]

$\therefore$ Exponent of 5 in 60!

$=⌊\frac{60}{5}⌋+⌊\frac{60}{5^{2}}⌋+⌊\frac{60}{5^{3}}⌋+$ .....

$=12+2+0+$ .....

$=14$

Exponent of 5 in 24!

$=⌊\frac{24}{5}⌋+⌊\frac{24}{5^{2}}⌋+⌊\frac{24}{5^{3}}⌋+$ ......

$=4+0+0$ ......

$=4$

Exponent of 5 in 36!

$=⌊\frac{36}{5}⌋+⌊\frac{36}{5^{2}}⌋+⌊\frac{36}{5^{3}}⌋+$ .......

$=7+1+0$ ......

$=8$

$\therefore$ From equation (1), exponent of 5 overall

$\frac{5^{14}}{5^{4}.5^{8}}.5^{3}=5^{k}$

$\Rightarrow 5^{5}=5^{k}$

$\Rightarrow k=5$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

solution.body:

and $b/2=\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}\Rightarrow b=\frac{8}{\sqrt{5}}$
